title: fix(service-job): enforce job timeouts in the durable run record (#7734)
body:
Fixes #7734

## Premise — verified against `origin/main` (`7a8476f`), holds exactly

The filer's root-cause analysis reproduces line for line on today's `main`:

- `db-job-adapter.ts:81` — `schedule()` builds `const wrapped = this.wrap(name, handler, 'schedule')` and hands **the wrapper** to `IntervalJobAdapter`/`CronJobAdapter` (lines 84–91) along with `options`.
- `interval-job-adapter.ts:157` / `cron-job-adapter.ts:158` — those adapters call `runWithPolicy(record.name, () => record.handler(...), record.options)`, i.e. the timeout guard wraps the **recorder**.
- `run-with-policy.ts:50` — `Promise.race([run(), guard])`. When the guard wins, `wrap()`'s own `await handler(ctx)` (line 200) is still pending on a handler JavaScript cannot cancel; whenever it resolves, line 211 writes `finishRun(runId, 'success', …)` over the run.
- The `timeout` verdict existed only in the in-memory `JobExecution` the adapters push (`interval-job-adapter.ts:171`), which `sys_job_run` never reads.
- `startRun` (line 233) hardcoded `attempt: 1`, for the same reason: the recorder ran once per attempt but had no way to know which attempt it was.

#7446's degraded-outcome mapping is intact on `main` and this change builds on it rather than replacing it — its whole suite stays green (see gates).

## The fix

**The party that observes the timeout is now the party that records it.**

1. `run-with-policy.ts` — `runWithPolicy` gains an optional 4th argument, a per-attempt `JobAttemptRecorder` (`onAttemptStart(attempt)` / `onAttemptSettled(attempt, result)`), where `result` carries `timedOut` reported at the instant the guard fires. The two former code paths (with/without `retryPolicy`) are unified into one loop so the recorder is driven identically either way; no-policy is simply `maxRetries = 0`.
2. `db-job-adapter.ts` — `wrap()` now runs the handler **under** `runWithPolicy` and records from those callbacks, instead of being run under someone else's policy. The timer adapter receives a registration with `retryPolicy`/`timeout` removed (`withoutPolicy()`), because the wrapper above it now applies both — forwarding them too would race the entire retry sequence against one more timeout budget and cut retries off mid-flight.

An abandoned attempt's late value loses `Promise.race` and reaches no observer, so **the overwrite has no code path left**. A per-run `settled` latch (one terminal write per `sys_job_run` row) is the second lock on the same door, so no future edit to this seam can move a run off a terminal status.

Behaviour changes, all on the durable record:

| | before | after |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `sys_job_run.status` for a timed-out run | `success` (or `running` until the handler resolved) | `timeout`, guard message in `error` |
| `sys_job_run.duration_ms` | the abandoned handler's full runtime | the abandoned attempt's |
| `sys_job.last_status` / `failure_count` | `success` / flat | `timeout` / **+1** — a run that never finished is a failure, and alerting keys on that count |
| `sys_job_run.attempt` | `1` on every row | the real attempt number (retry ⇒ `2`) |
| `replay()`'s synthetic row | mirrored only `degraded`; a timed-out replay paired an honest row with a `success` one | mirrors any terminal status |

**Additive**: a handler that finishes inside its timeout, or that declares no `timeout`/`retryPolicy`, records exactly what it did before. `runWithPolicy`'s existing 3-argument signature and retry semantics (throw-driven only) are untouched.

## Tests — `db-job-adapter.timeout.test.ts` (new, 10 cases)

Every assertion reads a `sys_job_run` / `sys_job` **cell**, never the in-memory history — the existing in-memory "records status 'timeout'" assertion stayed green all the way through this defect, which is exactly why it was not evidence.

- persists `status: 'timeout'`, not `success`; `last_status: 'timeout'` with `failure_count: 1`; `duration_ms` bounded below the handler's runtime
- **the overwrite race head-on**: guard fires → assert `timeout` → let the abandoned handler run to completion (asserting it really did resolve) → the row must still read `timeout`, still one row, `run_count`/`failure_count` unmoved
- retried timeout lands rows `[attempt 1, attempt 2]`, both `timeout`, `failure_count: 2`; a retried failure numbers `[1, 2, 3]`
- additivity: a handler inside its timeout still records `success` / `attempt 1`
- in-memory `getExecutions()` and the persisted row report the same verdict; `listExecutionsByStatus('timeout')` finds it
- replay of a timing-out job writes no `success` row
- the policy still applies through an **injected `CronJobAdapter`** — the guard against `withoutPolicy()` ever outrunning the wrapper that replaces it

**Reverse-verified**: with `db-job-adapter.ts` + `run-with-policy.ts` reverted to `origin/main` and the new test file kept, 9 of the 10 fail (`expected 'running' to be 'timeout'`, `expected [1,1] to deeply equal [1,2]`, …). The 10th is the additivity case, correctly green both before and after.
